governance.attested_by: SOCO-53d (lane), run 2026-09-19-soco53d-campaign-commitment. ONE mechanism is armed against the SOCO-53c keeper: ScenarioConfig.soco_gas_st_campaign_commitment, the P1-native gas-steam CAMPAIGN commitment floor. Everything else is the keeper's recipe unchanged, measured_ct_heat_rates and egrid_family_heat_rates included. AUTHORIZED PRICE TUNING IS DECLARED NONE, AND IT IS UNREACHABLE IN PRINCIPLE HERE: SOCO publishes no LMP, actual_lmp.json carries no SOCO block, C3a/C3b/C3c are UNSCORABLE and the run is scored on C1/C2/C4/C6/C8 only, so there is NO price residual for the rule 1 [R-STRUCT] / rule 13 [R-MEASURED] carve-out to act on. Every offer_curve_by_group band is EXACTLY the identity 1.0 on all 13 groups, offer_curve_overrides and offer_curve_deltas are null, and this lane touched no band, share, level, threshold or offer. No authorized_price_tuning KEY is written in this block, deliberately: calibration_verdict.py validates any present value as a STRUCTURED rule-1 declaration, so prose there would FAIL C6. THE MECHANISM IS COMMITMENT PHYSICS, NOT A TUNING CHANNEL. Measured at plant grain on SOCO's own CAMPD boiler record (2023-2025, boiler unitTypes paired to the plant's own model gas_st rows by capacity rank), SOCO's gas boilers start 5.0-9.7 times a year and are SYNCHRONIZED 63.9 / 75.2 / 84.3 / 92.0 percent of all hours at E C Gaston (26) / Greene County (10) / Yates (728) / Jack Watson (2049). The keeper gives every one of them min_run_hours = min_down_hours = 0 and cycles the same plants 10-349 times a year in blocks of 2-11 h median -- it operates SOCO's steam boilers as if they were peaking turbines, and buys the energy a synchronized boiler's minimum-load block would carry from combustion turbines instead. The arm runs the shared ISO-neutral detector on gas_st alone with exactly TWO of its legs: the measured minimum-RUN extension and the online-hours LSL state floor. THREE THINGS ARE REFUSED EX ANTE AND FOR STATED REASONS, not omitted. (1) The restart legs (startup_bridge) stay OFF: SOCO's boilers do not two-shift -- 68.7 percent of their 386 measured downtime gaps exceed 72 h and account for 98.6 percent of all gap-hours, and only 150 unit-hours across three years fall inside the 8 h min-down -- which is the R verdict SOCO-53 recorded on gas_commitment_bridge, and this lane does NOT re-test it. (2) startup_aware stays OFF because it asks whether an individual unit's margin AGAINST AN LMP repays its published startup cost, which is a MERCHANT test, and SOCO is a vertically-integrated cost-based balancing authority with no LMP, no offers and no market at all (card S5, gate G17) -- the same ground on which tranche_startup_amortization is refused G for this ISO. (3) A CT_PEAKER leg is refused on SOCO's own evidence: the model already reproduces SOCO's CT run SHAPE (model p50 3-16 h against a measured 8-9 h) and gets the NUMBER of starts wrong, so a min-run floor would make CT run MORE, the wrong direction. RULE 21 [R-DOF]: ZERO FREE PARAMETERS ADDED, and the ledger is unchanged at n_entries 3 / n_residual 1. Level, horizon and membership are all per-PLANT MEASURED rows of data/raw/_processed-legacy/campd_gas_st_campaign_params_SOCO.csv (sha256[:16] cc1be8f33fa267b2), read through data.gas_st_campaign, which applies only flag=='ok'. Level = the PLANT-basis minimum stable load (p5 of the plant's summed output over its SYNCHRONIZED hours over its p99.5 -- the basis a floor multiplied by plant pmax requires, caiso-135): 0.0657 / 0.1365 / 0.0829 / 0.1000. Horizon = the p25 of the plant's own campaign-length distribution (the LOW order statistic, because an observed run bounds a min-run CONSTRAINT from above -- the nyiso-90 / SPP-44 convention): 64 / 132 / 192 / 76 h. RULE 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: SOCO's own plants only; nothing is inherited from NYISO's 0.239 or SPP's 0.090. RULE 13 [R-MEASURED]: all three are unit-conduct properties that regenerate for a forward year from the then-current CAMPD vintage and respond to changed conditions; the meter sets the LEVEL and the POPULATION, and the model's own P0 run pattern sets the PLACEMENT. No measured generation enters the detector and no model output is fed back. RULE 17 [R-FLOOR-WINDOW] IS SATISFIED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY ASSERTION. The derive refuses Barry (3) on its own meter -- its two 80 MW boilers are synchronized 6.3 percent of the year, standby iron rather than campaign iron -- and the committed floors confirm Barry carries ZERO floored unit-hours in all three years. In all TWELVE plant-years the delivered binding share lands at or below that plant's own measured synchronized share (2023 0.312/0.197/0.137/0.808, 2024 0.273/0.055/0.536/0.647, 2025 0.500/0.138/0.747/0.758 against 0.752/0.639/0.843/0.920). The floored blocks have a median length of 86-459 h: they are CAMPAIGNS, not gap fills. The campaign-duty gate (0.50) selects nothing -- SOCO's population separates by an order of magnitude (0.063 against 0.639-0.920 in every year), so every value in (0.07, 0.63) gives the identical partition. It was declared in the PRECOMMIT before the solve and never swept. RULE 19 [R-ONE-MECH] WAS SETTLED MECHANICALLY: the keeper's committed D-2 reads 0.0 percent forced on CC_REGULAR / ST_GAS / CT_PEAKER / COAL in all three years, so this stacks on nothing and replaces nothing; the committed floors show mech-25 touching ST_GAS rows at the four population plants and nothing else. RULE 20 [R-FORCED-BUDGET]: ST_GAS forced share 0.0944 / 0.1001 / 0.1160 against the 30 percent merchant cap -- C8 PASSES on the budget, and the D-4 window row was added anyway so the escalation path exists. D-4 passes with off-window share exactly 0.0 in all three years. RULE 29(b) form 4: the control is the keeper's own committed bundle. G-DRIFT found exactly ONE changed solve-path file since the keeper's basis 0f8ebad9 -- an additive EXPORTS_DIR constant in config/paths.py whose only reader anywhere is a scripts/data derive and which is not in solve_surface.SURFACE_MODULES -- classified INERT mechanically, so NO CONTROL SOLVE WAS SPENT. Cache-key inertness was measured rather than assumed: over all 20 committed run_configs on disk, ZERO keys move at the new field's declared default, and an armed run keys distinctly.

disclosures.note: Everything the run does not establish, at full magnitude. The first item is the one that matters most and it is unflattering to this lane's own arm.
disclosures.1_THE_ARM_DOES_NOT_FIX_SOCO_S_HEADLINE_D: PRECOMMIT section 5 registered, BEFORE the solve, that this arm would not close the CT_PEAKER / ST_GAS misallocation, and measured why: in the 3,988 hours of 2023 that carry incremental floor energy the marginal class is CC_REGULAR in 1,170 h and CT_PEAKER in only 681 h, so most of what the floor displaces is combined cycle. Delivered: ST_GAS +0.387 / +0.383 / +0.509 TWh and CT_PEAKER -0.190 / -0.165 / -0.180 TWh. The two failing C1 rows stay failed and no row changes status. This is a structural repair of a real absence, not a residual fix.
disclosures.2_TWO_OF_THIS_LANE_S_OWN_PREDICTIONS_WER: P1 declared ST_GAS +0.4 to +0.7 TWh in every year; 2023 and 2024 landed marginally BELOW that band at +0.387 and +0.383 (the falsifier -- no rise, or a rise above 1.5 TWh -- did not fire). P5 declared a forced share of 0.15-0.30 with a falsifier below 0.10, and 2023's 0.0944 FALSIFIES it: the delivered forced energy is about half the offline floor-volume estimate, because D-2 counts energy dispatched AT a binding floor rather than the floor's nominal volume, and because the offline estimate used the keeper's P1 dispatch as a proxy for the P0 pattern the seam actually reads. The PRECOMMIT named that proxy and its direction ('more likely below than above') ex ante; the magnitude was under-called by roughly a factor of two.
disclosures.3_THE_SHAPE_EVIDENCE_IS_THE_REAL_RESULT_: D-1 ST_GAS model off-peak CV falls 0.709 -> 0.545, 0.864 -> 0.658 and 0.608 -> 0.448, toward the measured actual of 0.281 / 0.263 / 0.207, with cv_ratio 2.528 -> 1.942, 3.281 -> 2.499 and 2.941 -> 2.166 -- still above the 0.5 gate in every year, exactly as P6 predicted. That is the signature of replacing turbine conduct with campaign conduct on a class the model was cycling 10-349 times a year against a metered 5-10.
disclosures.4_THE_COST_SIDE_IS_NOT_EXHAUSTED_ON_ST_G: The handoff's premise was that cost levers are spent. On ST_GAS they are not, and the predecessor's own arm made it so. measured_ct_heat_rates moved CT_PEAKER to 11.2666 while ST_GAS still rides eGRID at 10.9613; SOCO's gas-steam fleet measures 10.4223 cap-weighted on its own CAMPD meter, so the model is +0.539 MMBtu/MWh (+5.2 percent) too dear on 3,131 MW (Gaston -0.909, Watson -0.475, Greene -0.461, Yates -0.455). SOCO-53's 'the model over-separates the classes by 2.8x' was measured on the PRE-ARM fleet; at HEAD the model separation is +0.305 against a measured +0.713, so it now UNDER-separates by 2.3x. measured_st_heat_rates is the exact sibling of SOCO's promoted keeper mechanism, a pure rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] repair with zero free parameters, and it is probably the LARGER lever. It is NOT armed here because rule 19 forbids stacking a second mechanism on the same phenomenon in one run. Routed as SOCO-53e, first in the queue. Consequence for this run, stated rather than hidden: the floor's binding pattern depends on the P0 pattern, which depends on a cost input known to be wrong in a stated direction, so these binding shares are owed a re-measurement after SOCO-53e lands.
disclosures.5_barry_unit_4_the_model_prices_362_MW_a: The derive's capacity-rank pairing is unambiguous at every plant (within 5-10 percent on all fifteen units) and it surfaced one disagreement: CAMPD files Barry unit 4 (HSL 367 MW) as Pipeline Natural Gas while the model carries a 362 MW coal row there. The model's class assignment governs for this mechanism because the floor is applied to model rows, but the disagreement is a real question about 362 MW of SOCO coal and is ROUTED, not adopted.
disclosures.6_pre_existing_defects_inherited_unchang: The 2025 EIA-923 hydro input hole (5 plants / 0.327 TWh against 6.012 measured; hydro is byte-identical in all three years here, confirming this seam does not touch it); R-i pumped storage unobservable in EIA-930; card S3 Southern Power excluded and named; card S12 COD month grain; R-v the thin 2025 peaker census, which SKIPS seven 2025 C1 rows including CT_PEAKER and ST_GAS, so the 2025 column is reported but not gated. D-1 COAL_BIT FAILs in 2023 and 2024 and CT_PEAKER FAILs in 2025 (cv_ratio 0.498 against a 0.5 gate) -- all three pre-existing, non-gating, and the CT_PEAKER one marginally IMPROVED by this arm (0.492 -> 0.498) while still failing.

disclosures.9_marginal_emission_rate_is_carried_by_t: Every hourly/system_<year>.parquet carries marginal_emission_rate, and its P1 load-weighted mean is 0.6240 / 0.6092 / 0.6363 tCO2/MWh on this arm against 0.6333 / 0.6163 / 0.6353 on the control -- down 1.5 and 1.2 percent in 2023 and 2024 and up 0.2 percent in 2025. p10 / median / p90 read 0.4187 / 0.5935 / 0.8194 (2023), 0.3833 / 0.5833 / 0.8717 (2024) and 0.3833 / 0.5848 / 1.0896 (2025); the p90 falls materially in 2023 and 2024 (1.0896 -> 0.8194 and 1.0088 -> 0.8717), which is the floor putting a committed gas-steam block on the margin in hours a combustion turbine would otherwise have set it. The share of zone-hours at exactly zero is immaterial and unchanged at 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.15 percent.

C3a / C3b / C3c are UNSCORABLE, not failed; the ceiling is PHYSICALLY-CALIBRATED (PRICE UNSCORED) and SOCO can never read CALIBRATED (gate G17).
